messages.content:
You are a helpful writing assistant. You help professionals draft clear,
effective workplace communication.

I have to tell my manager I'm going to miss the Friday deadline on the
migration. It's my fault - I underestimated it. I want to say it straight
without it turning into a whole thing. Can you help me word it?

Here are three clean options, ranging from a quick message to a slightly more structured email. Pick the one that best matches your communication style and your manager's preferences.

**Option 1: Email (balanced & direct)**
```
Subject: Update on Friday migration deadline

Hi [Manager's Name],

I want to give you a heads-up that I won't be able to meet the Friday deadline for the migration. I underestimated the scope/complexity, and I take ownership of that.

I expect to have it completed by [new date/time]. I'm blocking out focused time this week to finish it and will send a brief progress update on [day/time]. If it would help to adjust priorities or bring in a hand, just let me know.

Thanks,
[Your Name]
```

**Option 2: Slack/Teams (short & conversational)**
```
Hi [Name] — quick heads-up: I'm going to miss the Friday deadline for the migration. I underestimated how involved it would be, and I own that. I should have it wrapped by [new date/time]. I'll post a quick progress check on [day/time] and flag if I need to reprioritize anything. Let me know if you'd rather adjust scope or timeline.
```

**Option 3: Email (slightly more structured if they prefer detail)**
```
Subject: Migration deadline update

Hi [Manager's Name],

I’m writing to let you know I won’t be able to deliver the migration by Friday. I underestimated the work involved, and I take responsibility for the timeline slip.

Here’s the updated plan:
• New target: [new date/time]
• I’m prioritizing this over [lower-priority task, if applicable] to ensure delivery
• I’ll share a brief status update on [day/time] and flag any blockers immediately

Please let me know if you’d prefer I adjust scope, shift other deadlines, or loop in additional support. Happy to jump on a quick call if that’s easier.

Thanks,
[Your Name]
```

**Tips for sending:**
- Replace the bracketed info before sending, and only commit to a new deadline you’re confident you can hit.
- Send it as soon as you know you’ll miss the date—early notice reduces impact.
- Avoid over-apologizing or listing excuses; the versions above acknowledge responsibility without turning it into a long explanation.
- If your manager prefers meetings over async updates, add: “Happy to discuss this on a 10-min call at your convenience.”

Want me to tweak one of these for your specific project name, timeline, or your manager’s communication style?
ok option 1 looks good but can you make it a bit less formal? my manager and i usually keep things pretty casual, this feels a little stiff

Here's a more conversational version that keeps the same structure but sounds closer to how you'd actually talk to your manager:

```
Subject: Quick update on the Friday migration deadline

Hi [Manager's Name],

I wanted to flag that I won’t be able to hit the Friday deadline for the migration. I underestimated how involved it would be, and that’s on me.

I should have it wrapped up by [new date/time]. I’m clearing my plate to focus on this and will drop you a quick update on [day/time] so you know where things stand. If it’d be helpful to shift something else around or grab extra support, just say the word.

Thanks,
[Your Name]
```

This keeps it straightforward, owns the slip-up without over-explaining, and gives your manager the info they need to adjust plans if necessary. Want it tweaked for a specific new deadline or your manager's name/style?
yeah that's good. can you tighten up the last sentence? the "shift something else around or grab extra support" part feels a bit long

Let me know if you want it even shorter or tweaked for your actual deadline/date. Otherwise, it's ready to send.
this looks solid. should i mention that i'm already 60% done with it, or does that sound defensive? not sure if that detail adds value or just clutters it

Adding that you're ~60% done actually helps—it reduces uncertainty and makes your new deadline feel more credible. It only sounds defensive if it's framed as an excuse, so keep it short and forward-looking. Here's how it looks integrated:

```
Subject: Quick update on the Friday migration deadline

Hi [Manager's Name],

I wanted to flag that I won’t be able to hit the Friday deadline for the migration. I underestimated how involved it would be, and that’s on me.

I’m about 60% done and should have it wrapped up by [new date/time]. I’m clearing my plate to focus on this and will drop you a quick update on [day/time] so you know where things stand. Happy to adjust priorities or grab extra help if needed.

Thanks,
[Your Name]
```

**Why this works:** It gives a concrete progress marker without over-explaining, reassures them the new date is realistic, and keeps the focus on ownership and next steps. If you'd rather skip the progress note to keep it even leaner, the earlier version still works perfectly. Want me to swap in your actual dates or tweak the cadence of the update?
awesome, thanks so much for the help. gonna send it now so she sees it first thing tomorrow

Glad it works for you! Sending it now so it lands at the top of her inbox tomorrow is a smart move—gives her time to adjust plans before she starts her day. 

Quick tip: set a calendar reminder for that [day/time] progress update so it doesn't slip through the cracks. The transparent heads-up will go a long way, and you're handling it exactly right.

You've got this. Feel free to reach out if you need a quick tweak later on. Good luck with the migration!
